editorial:
Imagine your dad gets snatched by aliens, goes missing for three years, and then just pops back up on your doorstep. That is exactly what happens to young Tony. But here is the catch: his dad, Sam, is not exactly himself. He is more like a weird copy that does not understand how humans work. He tries to get back with his wife, Rachel, but she has already moved on with a new guy named Joe. The vibe is super strange and creepy, mixing a family drama with some really wild sci-fi elements that will leave you scratching your head in the best way possible.

What really makes this one a trip are the practical effects and the bizarre twists. The acting is okay, but the real star is the weirdness. While the pacing can feel a bit slow in the middle, the crazy payoff at the end makes it all worth it. If you love old-school creature features, you should definitely grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see all those gross effects in detail. If you are just browsing, try renting it on Apple TV for a fun movie night with friends who like weird cinema.
endingExplained: The big twist is that the man who returned was not actually Sam, but a clone made by aliens who didn't understand human biology. The clone starts acting crazy and eventually transforms into a giant, gross monster. In the final showdown, the monster is defeated, but it turns out the alien technology was trying to rebuild a human. It ends with a strange realization that the alien copies were just flawed experiments gone wrong.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s practical effects and strange alien stories.
